title: The 5 Most Powerful Rockets Ever Built, Ranked (#4 Went to the Moon)

scenes.text: The rocket that put humans on the Moon is only number four.

scenes.label: Falcon Heavy · 5M lb thrust
scenes.text: Number five: Falcon Heavy. Over five million pounds of thrust from twenty-seven engines, and its side boosters land themselves.

scenes.label: Saturn V · 7.5M lb thrust
scenes.text: Number four: Saturn V. Seven and a half million pounds. It's still the only rocket to carry people to the Moon.

scenes.label: SLS · 8.8M lb thrust
scenes.text: Number three: NASA's SLS. Eight point eight million pounds, built to send astronauts back to the Moon.

scenes.label: N1 · 10M lb thrust
scenes.text: Number two: the Soviet N1. Ten million pounds from thirty engines, but all four launches failed.

scenes.label: Starship · 16M+ lb thrust
scenes.text: Number one: SpaceX Starship. More than sixteen million pounds from thirty-three engines, twice the thrust of Saturn V.

description:
The five most powerful rockets ever built, ranked by liftoff thrust.
Falcon Heavy has over 5 million pounds, Saturn V 7.5 million, SLS 8.8 million, the Soviet N1 10 million, and Starship more than 16 million.
Did you expect Saturn V at number four?
